lead.headline: Wall Street loses $2.5tn as the Nasdaq falls 5.5% on fears a Democratic Congress will slow AI, but Indian shares keep rising
lead.short: The Nasdaq fell 5.5% on Thursday, wiping an estimated $2.5tn off US tech shares, as investors feared Democrats who campaigned against data centres will rein in AI. Nvidia fell more than 9% and AMD and Micron more than 17%. Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi fell 6% on Friday, but the Sensex was up 1.4% at 2pm.

why.text: Indian IT and chip-linked shares trade on the AI boom, and the money leaving US tech is now flowing into Indian shares.

more: The so-called magnificent seven lost about $1tn in a day. Tesla fell nearly 11% and SpaceX 8%, taking more than $300bn off Elon Musk's companies after he spent nearly $450m backing Republicans. Qualcomm fell 14% and Arm 15% after disappointing forecasts, and Micron paused plans for a plant in Taiwan. In Europe, Infineon fell more than 8.5% and ASML 6.5%.

Foreign investors bought ₹14,975 crore of Indian shares on Thursday, and the Sensex reached 80,391 at 2pm, its highest in three months, helped by Mahindra & Mahindra's 25% rise in quarterly profit. Smaller companies fell sharply, though, and the India VIX fear gauge jumped 9%. Brent was at about $98.

update.new: The AI sell-off has become a $2.5tn rout after the midterms.
update.front: The midterm result has turned worries about AI spending into the sharpest tech sell-off of the year.

seconds.headline: A Bengaluru cab driver is accused of killing his wife and six of her relatives, including a seven-year-old boy
seconds.short: Police in Bengaluru say Indushekar, a cab driver, killed his wife Sunita and six of her family at his home on 59th Cross in Srirampura, after a long dispute over her visits to her parents. The dead include her mother, two brothers, their wives and a seven-year-old nephew, Puneeth, whose body has been found.

why.text: It is one of the worst killings in the city in years, and most of the victims' bodies have not yet been found.

more: He first killed Sunita with a grinding stone and dumped her body near Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur district, police sources say, then switched off her phone and told neighbours she had gone on a trip. The next day he invited her brothers, Shivakumar and Shankar, to a party at his house and killed them.

He then killed their wives, both named Divya, his mother-in-law Roopavati, and Shankar's son Puneeth, police said. The couple had been married for about 20 years and argued often; he resented the support Sunita got from her family. The other bodies are believed to have been dumped at different places in and around Bengaluru. Rajajinagar police are investigating.

seconds.headline: Russell Brand is found guilty of rape and sexual assault and taken into custody before sentencing on Monday
seconds.short: A London jury found Russell Brand guilty on Thursday of one count of rape and three of sexual assault involving four women, from allegations dating back more than 20 years. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one of attempted indecent assault. Judge Joel Bennathan said Brand, 51, will be jailed when he is sentenced on Monday.

why.text: It is the biggest conviction of a British celebrity in years, and follows a 2023 documentary that first aired the claims.

more: A prosecutor called the comedian a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator". Brand denied the charges and testified that he was obsessed with sex as a young man and lived promiscuously but never forced anyone. The jury of eight men and four women at Southwark Crown Court deliberated for more than eight hours over two days.

His lawyers argued the women went to police only years later, after the 2023 documentary. Brand rose to fame in the early 2000s on television and BBC radio, appeared in Forgetting Sarah Marshall and was briefly married to Katy Perry. He has since moved to Florida and built a large online following.

facts.acquitted: two rapes, one attempted indecent assault

seconds.headline: Paraguay's president Santiago Peña resigns after a digital bank's collapse freezes the savings of 3 million people
seconds.short: Paraguay's president Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday after the collapse of Ueno Bank, which claimed about 60% of the country's adults as customers. The central bank put Ueno into resolution last week, freezing the deposits of 3 million customers and leaving many families without money for food. Lawmakers had voted unanimously that day to start impeachment proceedings.

why.text: It is a warning about digital banks that grow faster than their regulators can watch them.

more: "With my heart set on Paraguay and with the conviction that our republic must always come before any person or circumstance, I have decided to submit my resignation," Peña, 47, said in a video. In power since August 2023, he faced criticism over his past shareholding ties to the bank's owner. Bank executives have been arrested, and thousands protested outside Congress.

Ueno, bought in 2021 by the Grupo Vázquez conglomerate, became a digital bank with central bank approval at the end of 2023, under Peña's government. It grew fast on cash-back offers for groceries and sponsored the national football team. It came to hold $800m to $850m of deposits from state and pension bodies.

seconds.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber to vetted customers and rates it 'Critical' for cybersecurity risk, its highest level
seconds.short: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a model built to find and exploit security flaws, to a small group of vetted customers on Thursday, rating it "Critical" under its safety framework. OpenAI says its researchers used it to find 81 previously unknown Firefox flaws that Mozilla rated high-severity, and to build working exploits for 948 Linux kernel flaws, 588 of them new.

why.text: A model that can break into software at scale is now in the hands of companies, and attackers will want the same ability.

more: The model is meant to help security researchers find vulnerabilities, test how they could be exploited and fix them before attackers do. OpenAI raised its classification from "High" for GPT-5.6 Cyber. Mozilla has begun releasing fixes, and OpenAI says it has sent Linux maintainers proposed patches for the critical flaws.

It is available only to selected customers of Daybreak Red, OpenAI's access tier for authorised work such as penetration testing and exploit development. The company says it is seeing more attempts to misuse AI, including by malicious hackers and groups trying to copy its models. OpenAI also says it is ready to list its shares in 2027.

update.new: The model behind the Linux findings is out, rated Critical.
update.front: OpenAI has put a model it rates at its highest risk level into customers' hands.

stories.headline: The Supreme Court asks whether 'elite class' cars, not just stubble burning, are behind Delhi's toxic air
stories.short: "I hope you all are enjoying the weather in Delhi," Chief Justice Surya Kant said as the Supreme Court took up the capital's air pollution on Friday. The bench asked whether the affluent and their private vehicles were a major cause alongside stubble burning, and said the price paid for crop stubble should be announced well in advance.

why.text: The court is the one body that keeps pressing the governments on Delhi's air, and it is now looking at cars as well as farms.

more: Amicus curiae Aparajita Singh said pollution was hovering around the 'severe' band and that breathing the air was like smoking 30 cigarettes a day. She said stubble burning contributes 14% of Delhi's pollution, and that transport is the main source in the region. "Stubble, we keep on talking about... What about elite class people? Vehicles, high-end cars all operate," the bench said.

The Chief Justice said vehicle emissions are made worse by traffic, and that the more orders the court passes, the more cases of non-compliance follow: "It's simply human nature." The court said stubble management should be handed to gram panchayats. Delhi is under Stage II of its emergency plan, days before Diwali.

facts.bench: CJI Surya Kant, Justices Bagchi and Mohana

update.new: The Supreme Court takes up the crisis and questions vehicle emissions.

stories.headline: Investors say Anthropic's listing may be valued nearer $1tn than $1.5tn after the AI sell-off, and some want it delayed
stories.short: Three major investors planning to buy into Anthropic's listing believe its $1.5tn valuation must come down, The Wall Street Journal reports, with one suggesting about $1tn. The company has been aiming to list in the week before Thanksgiving and raise up to $100bn, more than SpaceX's record IPO in June. One investor raised the idea of postponing it.

why.text: The listing is the market's biggest test of faith in AI, and the sell-off has hit it a week before the roadshow.

more: One investor suggested Anthropic could raise about $80bn instead of $100bn. The company held $146.6bn in cash at the end of September. Executives and advisers are due to meet in the coming days to review the plans, and Anthropic has avoided firm commitments on structure and timing, the Journal says.

Reuters reported that potential investors were asking whether the roadshow planned for the week of 9 November could go ahead. Anthropic declined to comment. One prospective investor questioned whether institutions would add to AI holdings so soon after losses, even if markets recover. Companies in the Nasdaq Composite lost about $2.5tn in value on Thursday.

update.new: Investors question the valuation and timing after the sell-off.

stories.headline: Alcaraz plays Taylor Fritz in the Paris quarter-finals tonight after Berrettini pulls out with arm pain
stories.short: Carlos Alcaraz reached the Paris Masters quarter-finals without playing on Thursday when Matteo Berrettini withdrew with arm pain. He plays Taylor Fritz on Court Central at 23:30 IST tonight. Alcaraz has never gone beyond the quarter-finals in Paris, so a win would give him his first semi-final at the tournament.

why.text: It is his best chance yet at the one big indoor title he has never come close to.

more: Fritz beat Arthur Fils 6-3, 6-4 on Thursday and must beat Alcaraz to stay in the race for the ATP Finals in Turin, from 15 to 22 November. A win would lift him past Rafael Jodar and end Jodar's hopes; a defeat would knock Fritz out. Frances Tiafoe qualifies if Alcaraz or Ben Shelton wins.

Six players have qualified for Turin: Alexander Zverev, Alcaraz, Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli and Fils. Shelton plays Tommy Paul earlier on Court Central. Alcaraz's only match this week was a 7-6, 6-3 win over Alex Michelsen, five days after he won the title in Vienna.

update.new: Into the quarter-finals on a walkover; Fritz next.
